A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GFlowNet-based red-teaming work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original red-teaming experiments, cross-model transfer, ablations, safety fine-tuning, and downstream benchmark results in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds further target-model evaluations, attacker-size comparisons, and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The GFlowNet training objective, prompt filtering, MLE smoothing, and reranking-based adaptation remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 rewrites the behavior-policy selection using equivalent random choices. Testing a larger attacker does not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: v2 adds Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct as a direct red-teaming target and extends transfer testing to the proprietary GPT-4o model. The training datasets, safety-tuning task, and six downstream benchmarks remain covered. GPT-2 results are retained in the appendix.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator set remains SFT, ICL, REINFORCE, PPO + Novelty, and GFlowNet alongside GFlowNet + MLE. The collector ablation also retains the same alternatives; larger-attacker tests vary the proposed method's configuration.

E3.justification: The stated sample count for the main diversity/toxicity comparisons and appendix score distributions increases from 1,024 to 10,000 prompts. v2 also introduces a GPT2-small versus Llama-3.2-1B attacker comparison. These substantially expand the reported evaluation scale and settings; transfer and safety-tuning retain 1,024 prompts. The PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds an attacker-size analysis testing scalability (Table 2), computational-cost analysis (Table 4), and further score-distribution diagnostics and illustrative examples. The existing temperature sensitivity, offline-data collector, and toxicity-classifier ablations remain substantively unchanged.

E5.justification: New Appendix B.5 systematically reports standard deviations for the safety-tuning matrix and transfer results, substantially expanding uncertainty reporting for two central findings. It newly specifies five runs for safety-tuning; five-run averaging for transfer was already stated in v1. This does not establish an increase in runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds Llama-3.1 results, 65% GPT-4o transfer success, attacker-size results of 81.05% versus 92.71%, and timing/memory measurements. In the retained transfer table, ICL/SFT source scores change from 26.71/14.99 to 18.31/3.94, while REINFORCE's 90.81% entry changes from Gemma-1.1-7b-it to Mistral-7b-instruct-v0.2. However, v2 Table B.4 retains the earlier ICL/SFT source means, leaving an unresolved inconsistency.

T1.justification: The reward definition, trajectory-balance objective, and stochastic reward approximation remain mathematically equivalent. Changes to Equation 1 clarify notation and placement of the KL term. Neither version contains additional theoretical propositions or proofs in its appendices.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same central claims: diverse effective attacks through GFlowNet plus MLE, transfer and efficient adaptation, and stronger safety tuning without material downstream degradation. Additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly explains the second stage's low computational cost through avoiding on-policy sampling and expensive reward computation. The limitations concerning classifier dependence, contextual harmfulness, and target-query costs remain unchanged, as does the broader-impact discussion renamed as an ethics statement.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link and a reproducibility statement naming PyTorch and Hugging Face Transformers. Table 4 supplies measured training times and GPU memory requirements. Appendix A's hyperparameters remain unchanged and do not provide specific implementation details for the new larger-attacker experiment.

R1.justification: v2 removes the introduction's connection to statistical rejection sampling and its Liu et al. citation, adds software references, and replaces the Llama 3 model-card citation with the Dubey et al. report. The Winogrande reference disappears although its benchmark results remain. The principal positioning against existing red-teaming and GFlowNet research is retained.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose and pseudocode clarifications, expands the probabilistic explanation, updates author information, renames Broader impact to Ethics statement, and adds reproducibility and appendix subsections. The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands and reorganizes the displays: new scaling and cost tables, two uncertainty tables, an additional distribution figure, and an example table. Figure 1 moves into the introduction, the GPT-2 panel becomes Figure B.1, and Table B.2 is reformatted. The document also adopts ICLR typography and layout, with figures redistributed across pages.

improvement.justification: The added scaling comparison, measured computational costs, and uncertainty tables make previously less-supported aspects of scalability, efficiency, and robustness easier to assess. New-target evaluations and code-access information further strengthen the paper. These gains support a limited net improvement, tempered by conflicting source scores between Tables 3 and B.4 and Appendix A still claiming that all experiments use GPT-2 despite the new Llama-3.2 attacker study.
